question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $1$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & >-3y-1 \\ 8+1 & >-3y-1+1 \\ 9 & >-3y+0 \\ 9 & >-3y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-3.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}9\,\, & >\,\,-3y \\ \frac{9}{-3}\, & <\,\,\frac{-3y}{-3} \\ -3\, & <\,\,\frac{\cancel{-3}y}{\cancel{-3}} \\ -3\, & <\,\,y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's swap the left and right-hand sides so that the variable is on the left-hand side. Remember, we also need to flip the inequality.

$$
y>-3
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y>-3.$
